title: Discrete, Cationic Palladium(II)-Oxo Clusters via f-Metal Ion Incorporation and their Macrocyclic Host-Guest Interactions with Sulfonatocalixarenes

material_class.structural_family: cationic palladium(II)-oxo cluster (POC) with cubic {Pd6O12Ce8} core

synthesis.procedure: Pd6Ce8 was prepared by suspending PdCl2 (0.053 g, 0.3 mmol) and CeCl3·10H2O (0.064 g, 0.15 mmol) in 3 mL of 0.5 M sodium dimethylarsinate (cacodylate) buffer at pH 7 and heating at 80 °C with stirring for 1 h, during which the mixture became a deep-red solution with a brown-black precipitate. After cooling, the pH (4.5 after heating) was adjusted to 7.0 with 6 M aqueous NaOH, and the mixture was heated at 80 °C for a further 1.5 h. The cooled mixture was centrifuged (30 min, 3000 rpm), filtered, and left in an open vial to crystallize. Dark-red rod-shaped crystals formed after one week and were filtered and air-dried. Adding γ-cyclodextrin (0.05 mmol, 0.065 g) to the initial mixture reduced precipitation and increased the yield. The cacodylate buffer was prepared by titrating aqueous cacodylic acid with NaOH to pH 7.
synthesis.time: 1 h then 1.5 h heating; crystals after 1 week
synthesis.ph: initial buffer pH 7; pH 4.5 after first heating, then adjusted to 7.0
synthesis.vessel_or_method: stirred heating in aqueous buffer; centrifugation (3000 rpm, 30 min); open-vial crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: cool, centrifuge, filter, crystallize in an open vial; dark-red rod-shaped crystals filtered and dried in air
synthesis.yield: ~15% based on Pd (~25% based on Pd with γ-CD)

properties.summary: No magnetic data are reported for Pd6Ce8. The cluster shows strong intrinsic absorbance that prevents selective lucigenin excitation in indicator-displacement assays; host–guest binding with sulfonatocalixarenes was followed by ITC rather than cluster luminescence.

measurements.name: intrinsic absorbance (UV-vis)
measurements.value: large/strong cluster absorbance (no numerical λmax given in main text)
measurements.conditions: aqueous solution; interferes with LCG excitation in CX4 indicator-displacement assay (Figure S11)
